title: Crossbeam prefetch vs on-stream mini-benchmark (scratch)
content:
Purpose
This is a scratchpad mini-benchmark comparing two runtime strategies for interactive, low-token-turn workloads: aggressive crossbeam prefetch (prewarm+predictive KV prefetch) vs on-stream incremental decode (no prefetch). Goal: surface practical latency percentiles and per-token cost delta for small conversational exchanges (avg 28 tokens per response) and identify which approach gives better user-visible p95/p99 while keeping $/1M tokens reasonable.

Status
- informal, exploratory run on internal staging cluster (4x A100-sxm4 nodes, mixed CPU tmux load).
- not exhaustive; single sweep across two model variants and two request patterns.
- next: replicate under dedicated node pools + simulate real client jitter.

Test matrix (single pass)
- Models: LlamaX-13B-quant (int4 Q2) and Mistral-7B-fp16
- Strategies: prefetch (crossbeam predictive prefetch + KV cache warm) vs on-stream (lazy load, no proactive fetch)
- Workloads: micro-convo (burst of 50 concurrent short sessions, each 3 turns, avg resp 28 tokens) and drizzle (sustained 500 QPS 1-token prompts)
- Measured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (ms), tokens/s throughput, dollars per 1M tokens (rough unit price from reserved pool estimate)

Test rig details
- Node config: 4x A100-sxm4 GPUs, driver 525, cuda 12.3, rdma off for staging, numa interleaved.
- Serving runtime: staging release v0.91-pre (single-threaded decode path for this experiment intentionally), prefetch agent v0.3.2 with lookahead=2, kv-cache-size=128MB/session.
- Client: synthetic harness with exponential inter-arrival noise (lambda tuned to target concurrency), measured on the server side from request arrival to final token emitted.
- Cost model: amortized cost per GPU-hour = $2.80 (reserved internal rate), plus marginal infra (storage, net) folded into 10% overhead. Convert to $/1M tokens using tokens/sec observed per GPU.

Raw numeric summary (micro-convo)
Note: numbers are medians across 3 runs; jitter +/- 5–12%

Model: LlamaX-13B-quant (int4)
Strategy: prefetch
p50: 62 ms
p90: 118 ms
p95: 180 ms
p99: 420 ms
tokens/s per GPU: 420
$ per 1M tokens: $24.8

Model: LlamaX-13B-quant (int4)
Strategy: on-stream
p50: 74 ms
p90: 156 ms
p95: 240 ms
p99: 780 ms
tokens/s per GPU: 390
$ per 1M tokens: $26.6

Model: Mistral-7B-fp16
Strategy: prefetch
p50: 48 ms
p90: 92 ms
p95: 140 ms
p99: 310 ms
tokens/s per GPU: 620
$ per 1M tokens: $16.8

Model: Mistral-7B-fp16
Strategy: on-stream
p50: 55 ms
p90: 118 ms
p95: 190 ms
p99: 640 ms
tokens/s per GPU: 580
$ per 1M tokens: $18.0

Quick ASCII latency sparklines (p95, lower is better)
LlamaX-13B-quant: prefetch [====---] 180ms | on-stream [-------] 240ms
Mistral-7B-fp16 : prefetch [===----] 140ms | on-stream [-----] 190ms

Observations
- Prefetch consistently reduces p90/p95 and dramatically reduces p99 (2x–3x improvement) in micro-convo bursts. The biggest wins are at tail percentiles where KV warm avoids cold decoding stalls.
- Throughput (tokens/s) is slightly higher for prefetch in these runs, likely due to reduced per-request overhead and better packing of KV cache hits.
- Cost per 1M tokens improves with prefetch (2%–8% improvement observed) because increased tokens/s amortizes the GPU-hour cost; however the delta is more pronounced on LlamaX quant (relative improvements larger) because the quantized kernel benefits more from cache locality.
- Mistral-7B shows overall lower $/1M tokens in absolute terms due to faster wall-clock throughput; it also benefits from prefetch but the relative tail improvement is smaller than LlamaX.

Edge case: drizzle workload (sustained 500 QPS, 1-token prompts)
- Prefetch overhead can become a liability when the request pattern is fully uniform and predictable: lookahead prefetch causes small excess compute that doesn't translate to user-visible savings, increasing energy draw by ~3% in this test.
- On-stream slightly wins in pure high-sustained tiny prompt workloads due to simpler control path and lower speculative memory churn.

Small table: delta between strategies (p95, p99)
Model | p95 delta (on-stream -> prefetch) | p99 delta
LlamaX-13B | 240 -> 180 = 25% reduction | 780 -> 420 = 46% reduction
Mistral-7B  | 190 -> 140 = 26% reduction | 640 -> 310 = 52% reduction

Interpretation & user impact
- For interactive chat where perceived latency matters, lowering p95 and p99 yields more than proportional user satisfaction gains. Prefetch strategy clearly helps for conversational bursts and multi-turn sessions (where KV reuse occurs).
- For high-throughput single-token workloads (search-style or embeddings-heavy pipelines), prefetch gives marginal or negative returns unless the prefetch agent is tuned aggressively (smaller lookahead, cost-aware abort).

Open questions / TODOs
- Re-run with rdma enabled and with dedicated node pools to validate the staging artifacts replicate (network and numa can change tail behavior).
- Sweep prefetch lookahead and kv-cache-size to find knee point where cost starts to increase for drizzle workloads.
- Add real-client traces (voice assistant 95th perc. jitter) to test jittered arrival patterns.
- Run on 8x H100 pool to measure kernel delta for LlamaX int4 (we expect more pronounced throughput gains on H100 due to int8/int4 kernel density).

Experiment notes (raw)
- Observed occasional 1.8x p99 spike on on-stream LlamaX where a session hit a small cold-start path (kernel dispatch + memory swap). Traced to session affinity churn in the preemption scheduler.
- Prefetch agent produced ~2–4MB of extra KV per session in worst-case; under heavy churn this increased memory pressure and triggered small GC that we need to instrument.

Recommendation (current)
- Default for interactive chat routes: enable crossbeam prefetch with conservative defaults (lookahead=1, kv-cache-size=64MB), monitor p99 and memory pressure heatmaps for first 48h.
- For small single-token steady workloads: keep prefetch disabled unless adaptive heuristic shows positive ROI.

Short action items
- [ ] Add rdma-enabled run to CI bench script (Ethan)
- [ ] Parameter sweep for lookahead and cache size (Maya)
- [ ] Create dashboard widget in console for "prefetch hit ratio" and "prefetch cost delta" (Priya)

Notes to self
- This is rough; keep runs reproducible: add exact commit hashes for runtime and model kernels in next iteration. Capture mlperf-style run card.

End of scratchpad.
